solutionSource.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

entries.clue: Money goes back and forth for essentials (5,5)

blocks.note: a sailing boat tacks, zigzagging to and fro against the wind

annotation.surface: Cash sloshing to and fro while someone pays for the basics.
annotation.walkthrough: Getting down to brass tacks means dealing with the essentials; 'goes back and forth' reads like cash changing hands but is a sailor's word.
annotation.definitionFit: Brass tacks are the basic facts of a matter, as in 'get down to brass tacks'.

entries.clue: Confused, Glen catches a couple of zeds in appropriate place (9)

indicatorNotes.catches: the glen catches the zeds, holding them inside
indicatorNotes.in: the result sits in the bed

blocks.note: first part of BED, the place for sleep
first part of DALE, a valley

annotation.surface: A muddled man called Glen dozing off somewhere suitable.
annotation.walkthrough: Zeds are the snores of a sleeper, so the 'appropriate place' for them is a BED. Glen is a man's name on the surface but a valley, DALE, in the wordplay.
annotation.definitionFit: Bedazzled means dazed and confused, as if by a bright light.

entries.clue: Language once used in a northern boxing match (7)

indicatorNotes.boxing: A and N put the match in a box, one on each side

blocks.note: a vesta is a short match

annotation.surface: Dialect heard long ago at a prize fight up north.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Boxing match' reads as one sport; split them and 'match' is a vesta, the old word for a wax match, boxed in by A and N.
annotation.definitionFit: Avestan is the ancient Iranian language of the Zoroastrian scriptures, no longer spoken.

entries.clue: Court raised point during judicial examination (8)

indicatorNotes.raised: in a down clue, raising a word writes it bottom to top
indicatorNotes.during: the point goes inside the examination

blocks.note: the nub is the central point

annotation.surface: A lawyer raising a point in the middle of a hearing.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Raised' looks like 'brought up in court', but here it turns NUB upside down.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: a tribunal is a body that sits in judgement, as a court does.

entries.clue: Co-star crediting fantastic person who hired her? (7,8)

indicatorNotes.fantastic: wild and unreal, so the letters are rearranged

annotation.surface: An actor thanking the wonderful person who got her the part.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Her' is the co-star herself, so the question mark flags a definition that leans on the surface: whoever hired an actress is the casting director.
annotation.definitionFit: A casting director chooses and hires actors for a film or play.

entries.clue: Part of the neck, namely the hair around it (6)

blocks.note: a ruff is a ring of feathers or hair around a bird's or animal's neck

annotation.surface: An anatomy note on the neck and the hair that grows around it.
annotation.walkthrough: SC is the abbreviation of Latin scilicet, 'namely'. 'It' points back to the neck, which a ruff encircles.
annotation.definitionFit: The scruff is the back of the neck, as when a cat is picked up by it.

entries.clue: Liberal politician taking a hit (4)

indicatorNotes.taking: the Liberal politician takes A in

annotation.surface: A Liberal MP taking a beating in the polls.
annotation.walkthrough: To lamp someone is British slang for punching them. 'Taking a hit' reads as one phrase; split it after 'a'.
annotation.definitionFit: Lamp is informal British for hit or thump.

entries.clue: Red meat course mostly terrible (9)

indicatorNotes.mostly: most of COURSE, with its last letter gone
indicatorNotes.terrible: the remaining letters are in a terrible state, so rearranged

blocks.note: COURS(E) with the E dropped, rearranged

annotation.surface: A restaurant review: rare meat, and a main course that was mostly awful.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Red meat' pulls as one phrase, but 'Red' alone is the definition, a red wine.
annotation.definitionFit: Lambrusco is a sparkling Italian red wine.

entries.clue: Islander from Lindisfarne set laminator up (7)

indicatorNotes.from: the letters are taken from inside the words
indicatorNotes.up: in a down clue, the letters read upwards

annotation.surface: Someone from the holy island of Lindisfarne setting up a laminating machine.
annotation.walkthrough: Lindisfarne, an island off Northumberland, tempts you to look for a northern islander, but the islander is from Malta.
annotation.definitionFit: A Maltese is a native of the island of Malta.

entries.clue: Profound touch barely registered in act of passion (4,4)

blocks.note: a kiss is also the lightest touch, as when one snooker ball just grazes another

annotation.surface: A meaningful touch that hardly shows, in a love scene.
annotation.walkthrough: The two halves contradict each other on purpose: a deep kiss is anything but barely registered.
annotation.definitionFit: A deep kiss is a passionate, open-mouthed kiss.

entries.clue: Mike Pence breaking law in disorder (6)

indicatorNotes.breaking: M and P break into the law, splitting it

blocks.note: M is Mike in the NATO alphabet
p is the abbreviation for pence

annotation.surface: The US vice president Mike Pence flouting the law.
annotation.walkthrough: The surface names one American politician; split him into Mike (M) and pence (P, as in pounds and pence).
annotation.definitionFit: To rumple is to disorder, as in rumpling hair or bedclothes.

entries.clue: Prize task is to display the sixth brightest star (4)

indicatorNotes.to display: the phrase puts the answer on show inside itself

annotation.surface: A competition challenge to spot a particular star in the night sky.
annotation.walkthrough: Stars in a constellation are named by Greek letter in order of brightness, and zeta is the sixth letter.
annotation.definitionFit: Zeta, the sixth Greek letter, labels the sixth brightest star of a constellation.

entries.clue: Ignorant, like many police officers patrolling centre of Swansea (10)

indicatorNotes.patrolling: the police walk round the letter, surrounding it

annotation.surface: A jibe that beat officers walking the streets of Swansea know nothing.
annotation.walkthrough: Police in uniform are uniformed; one extra N turns them ignorant. Swansea is a city in Wales.
annotation.definitionFit: Uninformed means lacking knowledge, ignorant.

entries.clue: Covering many miles working in large country house (4-5)

indicatorNotes.in: ON goes in, just after the L

blocks.note: a machine that is on is working
a grange is a country house with farm buildings

annotation.surface: Someone at work on a big estate who covers a lot of ground.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Large country house' reads as one phrase; the L comes off the front to make room for ON.
annotation.definitionFit: Long-range means reaching over a great distance, as in a long-range missile.

entries.clue: Setter penning Listener, although missing last piece of mechanism (9)

indicatorNotes.penning: the setter pens, or encloses, the rest
indicatorNotes.missing last: the final letter of WHEN is dropped

blocks.note: first letter of GEL, which sets hair
WHEN (as in 'why walk when you can drive?') without its N

annotation.surface: A crossword setter writing for the Listener puzzle but lacking the final piece.
annotation.walkthrough: The Listener is a famous Times crossword, so 'Setter' seems to mean the compiler; here it is hair gel. WHEN can mean although, as in 'he stayed when he could have left'.
annotation.definitionFit: A gearwheel is a toothed wheel in a machine.

entries.clue: Residue from parties initially ignored (5)

indicatorNotes.initially ignored: the first letter is left out

annotation.surface: The mess left after parties that nobody noticed at first.
annotation.walkthrough: A bash is informal British for a party; take off its first letter.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: what is left when a fire burns out is the ashes.

entries.clue: Only home with motorway running through it is extremely awe-inspiring (9)

indicatorNotes.running through: the motorway runs through the middle, splitting the words

annotation.surface: A lament that the one house with a motorway through it is truly impressive.
annotation.walkthrough: British motorways are numbered M1, M25 and so on, so M is a motorway.
annotation.definitionFit: Solemnest is the superlative of solemn, which can mean awe-inspiring.

entries.clue: Weed in toilet and basin when drunk (8)

blocks.note: the can is slang for the toilet

annotation.surface: Someone drunk finding weed in the loo and the sink.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Weed' could be any garden plant, but in the surface's bathroom full of drunks it is the drug.
annotation.definitionFit: A slang sense: 'weed' is an everyday nickname for the drug.

entries.clue: Democrat sometimes called Republican in west coast city (5)

annotation.surface: A US politician who gets labelled the other party's man in a West Coast city.
annotation.walkthrough: Democrat and Republican set you in America, where 'West Coast' means California; the city is on the west coast of Africa.
annotation.definitionFit: Dakar is the capital of Senegal, on Africa's Atlantic coast.

entries.clue: Nation’s poet loses pound of gold (7)

indicatorNotes.loses: whatever the poet loses is no longer part of him, so the L drops out of LAUREATE

blocks.note: LAUREATE without L, the pound sign

annotation.surface: The national poet going broke.
annotation.walkthrough: The Poet Laureate is Britain's official national poet; L stands for a pound, from Latin libra.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym from Latin aurum, gold: aureate things are golden.

entries.clue: In denial, slag off A & E loudly, perhaps (9)

indicatorNotes.loudly: the words are said out loud

blocks.note: A, and E perhaps, a vowel, spoken

annotation.surface: Someone refusing to admit they rubbished the hospital casualty department.
annotation.walkthrough: A & E is a British hospital's Accident and Emergency department; here A is just A, and E is an example of a vowel.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: to disavow something is to deny any link with it.

entries.clue: Amount of distortion in part of book about conflict? (7)

annotation.surface: How much a history book bends the truth about a war.
annotation.walkthrough: Read the wordplay as 'a page about war': the question mark admits the split is loose.
annotation.definitionFit: Warpage is the extent to which something is warped.

entries.clue: Outlet for one topless outfit (6)

indicatorNotes.topless: the first letter, the top in a down clue, comes off

annotation.surface: A shop selling topless outfits.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Topless outfit' sounds racy but only means dress without its first letter.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: both words name a way for something to get out.

entries.clue: Where one might find Jack bragging about space that one’s left (5,5)

indicatorNotes.one’s left: I (one) has left, gone out of the word

blocks.note: an en is a printer's space

annotation.surface: Jack showing off about a flat he has just moved out of.
annotation.walkthrough: Jack looks like a man, but it is the small white ball bowlers aim at, and a crown green is a lawn for bowls with a raised middle.
annotation.definitionFit: The jack is the target ball in bowls, played on a green such as a crown green.

entries.clue: Unpleasant smut curtailed (4)

indicatorNotes.curtailed: its tail, the last letter, is cut off

annotation.surface: Filthy talk, cut short because it is nasty.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Smut' suggests dirty jokes, but it is literal dirt, grime.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: a grim task or prospect is a thoroughly nasty one.

entries.clue: Next to empty temple, shot animals for egg cell? (6)

indicatorNotes.Next to: the game is placed beside the temple's remains
indicatorNotes.empty: the word is emptied of its middle letters

blocks.note: game is animals hunted and shot

annotation.surface: Beside a deserted temple, hunters shooting animals for their eggs.
annotation.walkthrough: The question mark marks the egg cell as one example: a sperm cell is a gamete too.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by example: an egg is one kind of sex cell, the sperm being the other.

entries.clue: Order policeman to leave mate following cigarette (8)

indicatorNotes.to leave: the policeman is told to leave, so COP walks out of COPULATE
indicatorNotes.following: what is left comes after the cigarette

blocks.note: tab is slang for a cigarette

annotation.surface: An order for a policeman to leave his friend behind after a smoke.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Mate' looks like a friend but is the verb, to copulate, and the policeman is the COP that leaves it.
annotation.definitionFit: To tabulate is to put data in order in a table.

entries.clue: Dreadful place cut short welcome (4)

indicatorNotes.cut short: the last letter is cut off

annotation.surface: A horrible venue that gives visitors a curt greeting.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Welcome' is a noun or verb on the surface, but here it is the greeting HELLO.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym by exaggeration: any awful place gets called hell.

entries.clue: Start to suspect terrible setter’s extremely self-confident in examination (6,4)

annotation.type: charade + anagram + first letter + outer letters

indicatorNotes.terrible: the setter's letters are in a terrible state
indicatorNotes.extremely: only the extreme letters of self-confident

annotation.surface: Suspicion that a bad crossword setter is far too cocky in an exam.
annotation.walkthrough: The setter's 'S counts in the anagram, and 'extremely' takes just the two ends of self-confident.
annotation.definitionFit: A stress test is an examination of how a system, heart or bank copes under strain.
